Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Burlington VT
132 PM EDT Sat Sep 26 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
As of 1047 AM EDT Saturday...

A Lake Wind Advisory has been issued for the Broad Waters and
Southern Waters of Lake Champlain. See Marine Section for more
details.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 233 AM EDT Saturday...

1. A Nor'easter will continue to move along the coast, bringing 
chances for showers and breezy winds this weekend, but the strongest 
impacts will remain over southern New England. 

2. Seasonable, mainly dry weather continues through late week

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 233 AM EDT Saturday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: A Nor'easter centered off the Mid-Atlantic coast will be 
the main weather feature this weekend, with our region on the 
periphery of the system and more impactful weather further south 
towards the coast. Several rain bands will move across southern 
Vermont and try to make their way further north, but drier air 
across the region will limit their progress and how much 
precipitation is expected. Throughout the weekend, southern Vermont 
will see the most precipitation after several rounds of showers, but 
further north look to remain drier. The system will slowly exit the 
region later this weekend into the start of next week, bringing 
greater precipitation chances for Sunday into Monday before drier 
conditions return towards Tuesday. 

In addition to the precipitation, a strong jet looks to bring gusty 
winds to the region, particularly tonight into Sunday, with the 
greatest concern across the western slopes in southern Vermont and 
summit levels. Temperatures will be on the cooler side as well, 
especially for Sunday and Monday with clouds and periods of showers 
expected, especially across southern and eastern Vermont.

KEY MESSAGE 2: No impactful weather is expected for the middle to later 
portions of next week. The Nor'easter currently affecting southern 
New England and the Mid-Atlantic region will exist in a much 
weakened state by Tuesday night and be in the process of exiting 
northeast into the westerlies away from our region as skies trend 
partly cloudy. Thereafter, weak high pressure mainly controls 
regional weather conditions for the Wed-Thu time frame with daily 
highs warming into the upper 60s to lower 70s. This morning's GFS 
depiction of a rather sharp northern stream trough feature and 
scattered/numerous showers passing through the area Wednesday 
evening appears overdone. This solution has little support from 
other output which seems reasonable given weak baroclinicity evident 
in 925-850 hPa thermal profiles and I've offered mainly a dry 
weather through this time frame. By Friday a somewhat more 
pronounced cold front appears poised to swing through the region. 
Again, moisture is rather starved with this feature, so 
precipitation chances will be generally held in the 20-40% range. 
Behind the front, slightly cooler air arrives for next weekend, but 
values should remain within 5 degrees of seasonal early October 
norms.

&&

.AVIATION /18Z SATURDAY THROUGH THURSDAY/...
Through 18Z Sunday...No aviation impacts through the day today.
Clouds will slowly lower in the overnight hours as the nor'easter
currently off the coast of New Jersey approaches our CWA. As the
system approaches, we will see increasing wind shear especially at
RUT and MPV. Ceilings will lower to MVFR for our southern terminals
by tomorrow morning. RUT could see some periods of heavier rain
during the day tomorrow, but other terminals should see only light
rain and minimal impact.

Outlook...

Sunday Night: Mainly VFR, with local MVFR possible. Chance SHRA.
Monday: Mainly MVFR, with local IFR possible. Likely SHRA.
Monday Night: Mainly MVFR, with local IFR possible. Chance SHRA.
Tuesday: Mainly MVFR, with local IFR possible. NO SIG WX.
Tuesday Night: MVFR/IFR conditions possible. NO SIG WX.
Wednesday: Mainly VFR, with areas MVFR possible. Slight chance
SHRA.
Wednesday Night: VFR. Slight chance SHRA.
Thursday: Mainly VFR, with local MVFR possible. Slight chance
SHRA.

&&

.MARINE...
A Lake Wind Advisory is in effect for the southern waters and
the broad waters of Lake Champlain. Winds will increase today to
15 to 25 knots, with gusts to 30 knots, especially over 
southern portions of the lake. Winds will build to 1 to 3 feet
today, highest over southern Lake Champlain. Winds and waves
will peak overnight tonight at 20 to 30 knots with waves 2 to 4
feet, especially in the early morning hours on Sunday. Winds
will diminish through the day Sunday, becoming around 10 knots
by the evening. Waves will also subside to 1 to 3 feet by Sunday
evening, then further subside to 1 to 2 feet Sunday night. 

Winds will be lighter and waves lower further north over the
northern waters of Lake Champlain, where winds will peak around
20 knots tonight and waves will stay in the 1 to 2 foot range.

&&

.BTV WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
VT...None.
NY...None.

&&

$$
